body: Forward test of the sector cycle/lead indicator method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.35 (naive base rate 0.30) that: Bharti Airtel announces a headline prepaid mobile tariff increase (≥10% on its core unlimited plans) by 30-Jun-2027. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): ARPU ₹271 (from ₹264); India mobile ~51% of revenue; consolidated EBITDAaL ~₹31,500 cr (51.7%), net debt/EBITDAaL ~0.70; ~₹2,900 cr spent on a data-centre land parcel. Management: 'long-term ARPU growth ultimately depends on a more rational pricing structure where the industry is able to monetize the continued growth in data consumption'; the Q2 'intervention… on prepaid ladder' (discontinuing the ₹299 pack) was 'experimentation on our own base'; 'the architecture correction is a much broader correction that is required in the industry… to move more decisively'. Reasoning: Cycle: Indian telecom takes a headline hike every ~2–2.5 years (Dec-2019, Nov-2021, Jul-2024 — from memory, unverified); by mid-2027 the gap would be ~3 years and capex for 5G/data centres keeps pressure on. But Airtel is talking about 'architecture' (data monetisation) rather than a flat hike, and the leader's timing is unknowable. Slightly above base. Resolution: YES if, between 21-Nov-2026 and 30-Jun-2027, Bharti Airtel announces (press release, NSE filing or widely reported company statement) increases to its prepaid mobile tariffs under which its most popular 28-day unlimited plan price rises ≥10%. Plan withdrawals, validity cuts or postpaid-only changes = NO. Source: Bharti Airtel press releases / NSE announcements; national press coverage. Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: With headline hikes roughly every 30 months, the chance one falls in any given ~7-month window is ~25–30%.
